steps.title: Generate guide RNA DNA template
steps.instruction: Set up a 20 µL PCR with 4 µL 5× Phusion HF Buffer, 0.8 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 0.4 µL universal forward primer (100 µM), 0.4 µL target‑specific reverse primer (100 µM), 0.2 µL Phusion DNA polymerase, and 14.2 µL molecular water; run 35 cycles (95 °C 30 s initial, then 95 °C 10 s denature, 57 °C 10 s anneal, 72 °C 10 s extension) followed by 72 °C 2 min final extension and hold at 4 °C 2 min; verify product (66 bp) by electrophoresing 2 µL on a 2 % agarose gel; ensure correct oligo concentrations; purification is not required.

steps.title: In vitro transcribe guide RNA
steps.instruction: In a 20 µL reaction combine 2 µL 10× HiScribe T7 Reaction Buffer, 2 µL each of ATP, GTP, CTP and UTP (100 mM), 8 µL prepared DNA template, and 2 µL T7 RNA Polymerase Mix; incubate at 37 °C for 8–18 h; expected yield ≥50 µg RNA.

steps.title: Assemble Cas12a RNP complex
steps.instruction: In a 0.2 mL PCR tube combine 0.34 µL LbCas12a protein (100 µM, ≈5 µg), x µL gRNA (≈0.5 µg; e.g., 0.5 µL if gRNA is 1000 ng/µL), 2 µL 10× NEBuffer 2.1, and molecular water to a final volume of 20 µL (water volume = 17.66 µL – x); add the protein last to avoid precipitation; incubate 15 min at 25 °C; use the RNP immediately for protoplast transformation.

steps.title: PCR amplify donor DNA
steps.instruction: Set up a 50 µL PCR with 10 µL 5× Phusion HF Buffer, 1 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 2.5 µL each of no‑homology HYG forward and reverse primers (10 µM), 0.5 µL Phusion DNA polymerase, 1 µL pFGL821 plasmid (≈5 ng/µL) as template, and 32.5 µL molecular water; run 30 cycles (98 °C 30 s initial, then 98 °C 10 s denature, 57 °C 30 s anneal, 72 °C 1 min extension) followed by 72 °C 10 min final extension and hold at 4 °C 2 min; expected amplicon size 1,466 bp; each transformation requires ≈3 µg donor DNA, so scale the number of reactions accordingly.

steps.title: Check donor PCR product
steps.instruction: Run 2 µL of the PCR product on a 1 % agarose gel; a single band at 1,466 bp indicates successful amplification.

steps.title: Purify donor DNA
steps.instruction: Purify the PCR reaction using the Wizard® SV Gel and PCR Clean‑Up System (Promega) according to the manufacturer’s protocol; if multiple bands are present, perform gel extraction with the same kit to isolate the correct product.

steps.title: Quantify and store donor DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration with a NanoDrop; aim for 200–350 ng/µL; store the purified donor at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Prepare lysing solution
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh protoplast lysing solution as described in the “prepare medium and stock solution” section (details not provided in this excerpt).

steps.title: Collect and wash mycelia
steps.instruction: Filter sub‑cultured liquid CM through two layers of 6½ in. Disks Non‑Gauze Milk Filter paper into a funnel, collect the mycelial mat, and wash with 5 mL 1× STC solution.

steps.title: Digest mycelia for protoplasts
steps.instruction: Transfer the washed, dry mycelia to a 100 mL flask containing 25–30 mL lysing solution; shake at 30 °C, 70–80 rpm, in the dark for 2.5–3 h, manually breaking up the mycelial mass to improve enzyme access.

steps.title: Check protoplast digestion
steps.instruction: Examine an aliquot under a dissecting microscope with a hemocytometer; healthy protoplasts indicate successful digestion, whereas abundant undigested mycelium requires longer incubation (avoid over‑digestion which causes collapse).

steps.title: Filter and wash protoplasts
steps.instruction: Pass the digestion mixture through two layers of Miracloth into a pre‑chilled 50 mL Falcon tube; rinse the Miracloth residue with additional 1× STC to recover all protoplasts.

steps.title: Centrifuge protoplasts (first)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 4 °C, 5,000 rpm (≈3,829 g on a Beckman Coulter‑Allegra 25R) for 10 min; a visible pellet should form.

steps.title: Resuspend protoplast pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant into biohazard waste and gently resuspend the pellet in 5–10 mL 1× STC by pipetting or flicking.

steps.title: Centrifuge protoplasts (second)
steps.instruction: Repeat the centrifugation at 4 °C, 5,000 rpm for 10 min.

steps.title: Finalize protoplast concentration
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL 1× STC, count protoplasts with a hemocytometer and adjust the suspension to 8 × 10⁶–5 × 10⁷ protoplasts/mL with additional 1× STC; aliquot 200–250 µL into individual 50 mL Falcon tubes; optionally add 7 % v/v DMSO and freeze at –80 °C for later use.

steps.title: Prepare extraction tubes
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, place 1.0 mm glass beads, 400 µL 1 M KCl, and 400 µL chloroform into each 2 mL screw‑cap tube.

steps.title: Add plug and homogenize
steps.instruction: Add a fungal plug (~1 cm diameter) to each tube, then homogenize at power setting 4 for 6 cycles of 30 s each to disrupt the tissue.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenized tubes at 13,200 rpm (≈16,100 g on an Eppendorf 5415D) for 10 min.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Pipette 200 µL of the upper aqueous phase into a new labeled tube.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Add 120 µL isopropanol to the transferred supernatant, mix well, and incubate ≥10 min (in the hood) to precipitate DNA.

steps.title: Centrifuge DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13,200 rpm for 10 min; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 500 µL 75 % ethanol, then centrifuge again at 13,200 rpm for 10 min; discard the ethanol.

steps.title: Air dry pellet
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the DNA pellet for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL sterile water to dissolve the DNA pellet; use 1 µL of this solution as template for downstream PCR genotyping.
